{/* @license CC0-1.0 */}

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/checkbox.tokens.json";

import * as CheckboxStories from "./Checkbox.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={CheckboxStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={CheckboxStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use Checkboxes for one or multiple choices that do not exclude each other.
Each Checkbox operates independently of other Checkboxes in a list at the same hierarchical level.
Checking an additional Checkbox does not affect other selections in that list.

Use a Checkbox to answer a closed question if multiple answers are possible.

Use a group of Checkboxes to filter data on a page, in a menu, or within a component.

A Checkbox can also be used for bulk selection or deselection of an entire list of Checkboxes.
Still, it should be clear that the bulk selection Checkbox is at a different hierarchical level than the list being fully selected or deselected.

### When not to use

Use a [Radio](/docs/components-forms-radio--docs) when a user can select only one option from a list.

### How to use

Wrap a list of Checkboxes in a Field Set with a legend describing what the list is about.
For example, if the Checkboxes are used to get answers to a question, the legend is the question.

### How to write

A label starts with a capital letter.
It does not have punctuation at the end if it is a single sentence, word, or fragment.
It is written in the first person when asking the user to agree to the terms and conditions.

## Examples

### Long label

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.LongLabel} />

### In a Field Set

Use a Field Set to group several Checkboxes with a legend, description and / or an Error Message.

Because of an [NVDA bug](https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/12718), we add the description text to the Field Set with `aria-labelledby`,
instead of `aria-describedby`.
Screen reader users will no longer be able to skip the description, but we think that is preferable to missing the description entirely.
The order of the `id`s is the order in which they are read by screen readers.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-labelledby` and `id` attributes from the Field Set.

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in descriptions. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-field--docs#no-rich-text).

Check [the Field Set docs](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.InAFieldSet} />

### In a Field Set with validation

A Field Set with Checkboxes can become invalid.
In this case, connect an Error Message to the Field Set.
Because of [the NVDA bug mentioned earlier](https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/12718),
we add the Error Message text to the label as well.
Add an `aria-labelledby` attribute to the Field Set and provide the `id` of Error Message as its value.
The order of the `id`s is the order in which they are read by screen readers.

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in an Error Message. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs#no-rich-text).

Check [the Field Set docs](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.InAFieldSetWithValidation} />

### With custom icon

Replace the icon with a custom version to use the Checkbox in a different theme or visual identity.
Use `ams-checkbox__rectangle`, `ams-checkbox__hover-indicator`, `ams-checkbox__checked-indicator`
and `ams-checkbox__indeterminate-indicator` classes in its SVG markup.
Websites for the City of Amsterdam must use the default icon.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.WithCustomIcon} />

## Design

A list of Checkboxes is vertically stacked to enhance readability and usability.

The box is drawn as an SVG inside the label rather than by the browser, which is what makes a custom icon possible at all and keeps the control identical across browsers.
It carries a separate ring that appears on hover, so the box grows a halo instead of changing size or colour.

The box and the label sit in one line box that never breaks between them, and the label may wrap onto as many lines as it needs beside it.

Checked, indeterminate, invalid and disabled each change one thing: the fill, the mark inside, the outline colour, or the text colour.
The states can therefore combine — an invalid checked box, a disabled indeterminate one — without any pair of them fighting over the same property.

In forced colours mode the drawing is redone in system colours: the box takes the field colours, a selected one the active text colour, and a disabled one the greyed text colour.
The fills the tokens set are ignored there, so without this a checked box and an empty one would look the same.

## Accessibility

A Checkbox renders a native `input` inside a `label`, so the whole label is the target and the browser supplies the role, the checked state and the keyboard behaviour.

The input is not hidden away: it is reduced to no width, which keeps it focusable, announced, and submitted with the form.
Its focus ring is moved onto the label so the ring surrounds the box and its text rather than a control with no size.
Browsers without support for the modern focus rules show that ring for every focus, including a click, which is the safer way round.

The indeterminate state is a visual and programmatic state of the checkbox itself, not a third value.
A form submits it as unchecked, so a bulk-selection box in that state says something about the list below it and nothing about its own value.

The invalid styling responds to `aria-invalid="true"` and to the browser’s own `:invalid` state alike.

## See also

- [Radio](/docs/components-forms-radio--docs) – when a user can select only one option from a list.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – groups several Checkboxes with a shared legend.

## Design tokens

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/date-input.tokens.json";

import * as DateInputStories from "./DateInput.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={DateInputStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={DateInputStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Date Input when the user must enter a calendar date and the date picker provided by the browser is appropriate.

### When not to use

When asking for a date that is easy to remember or find, like a birthday or passport expiration date,
use a Field Set with separate Text Inputs for day, month, and year.
This approach is easier to use than using a Date Input component.

For more information on this pattern, see the [gov.uk](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/date-input/) and [NL Design System](https://nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/wanneer-welk-form-element/iedereen-kan-invullen) documentation.

Avoid disabling input fields.
They cause usability and accessibility problems.
Disabled fields are often skipped by screen readers.
This makes it hard for users who rely on assistive technologies to understand the form’s content.
They are not included in form submissions, which can lead to incomplete or missing data.

Alternatives:

1. Use the `readonly` attribute.
   This makes a field uneditable but keeps it accessible and included in form submissions.
2. Display data as plain text or within a non-input element like a `span` or `div`.
3. Use conditional logic to hide or show fields based on user interaction.
   This ensures all necessary fields are accessible and editable when needed.
4. Use a label or text to explain why a field is not editable if you must disable it temporarily.
   This helps the user understand the context.

### How to use

Wrap a Date Input in a Field to associate it with a Label, description, and Error Message.

## Examples

### Memorable date

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.MemorableDate} />

### Memorable date with validation

To show validation errors, add `invalid` and an [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) to the Field Set.
Make sure to connect the Error Message to the Field Set, otherwise this won’t be read by a screen reader.
Additionally, apply the `invalid` prop to the Text Inputs to visually indicate the error.
Only use the `invalid` prop on Text Inputs that have errors.
For example, only mark the ‘year’ input as invalid if the year is not provided.

See the [gov.uk](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/date-input/#error-messages) documentation on validation for this pattern.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.MemorableDateWithValidation} />

### Date and time

To let the user select a specific time on a date, use the `datetime-local` type.
Note that the control’s UI varies in general from browser to browser.

The value represents a local date and time, not necessarily the user’s local date and time.
In other words, the input allows any valid combination of year, month, day, hour, and minute – even if such a combination is invalid in the user’s local time zone.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.DateTime} />

### Invalid

Indicates that the input value does not meet the specified constraints.
An [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) must be displayed above the field.
To highlight the error even more, the parent [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) component’s `invalid` prop must also be set.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.Invalid} />

### Disabled

A field that can not (yet) be used is indicated with a grey border.
It will not respond to interactions, e.g. with the mouse or keyboard.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.Disabled} />

### In a Field

Use a Field to group a Date Input with a Label, description and / or an Error Message.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Date Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.InAField} />

### In a Field with validation

If the Date Input can become invalid, add an Error Message and its `id` to the `aria-describedby` attribute of the Date Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={DateInputStories.InAFieldWithValidation} />

## Design

This component uses a native date input, which is styled differently in different browsers and operating systems.
Recreating the native functionality is quite difficult and prone to accessibility errors, which is why we’ve chosen not to do that.
This does mean that this component does not look identical on all browsers and operating systems.

The styling therefore stops at the box: the border, the padding and the type are ours, and the segments inside it, the format hint and the calendar that opens belong to the browser.
Chromium lets its calendar button be replaced, so there it carries our icon; other browsers keep their own.

The field is given a minimum width and height.
A native date field is much smaller when empty than when filled on some devices, and without a floor a form would visibly resize as it was completed.

Everything else — the border, the padding, the type, and the invalid and disabled states — matches a [Text Input](/docs/components-forms-text-input--docs), so a date sits level with the other fields of a form.

## Accessibility

A Date Input renders a native `input` of a date type, so screen readers announce it segment by segment and every browser’s own keyboard handling applies: arrow keys to change a part, typing to fill one, and the browser’s picker for those who prefer it.
That behaviour is the reason for using the native control rather than rebuilding it.

The format the field shows and expects comes from the browser and the operating system, not from the language of the page.
A visitor whose browser is set to another locale sees the order of day, month and year they are used to, which is helpful — but it also means the page cannot promise which one they will see.

The invalid styling responds to `aria-invalid="true"` and to the browser’s own `:invalid` state alike.
The second matches a partially entered date as well, so a field can turn red while someone is still filling in its segments; set `aria-invalid` from your own validation to control when that happens.

## See also

- [Calendar](/docs/components-navigation-calendar--docs) – navigate between dates using a calendar view.
- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a single input with its Label, description, and Error Message.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – use with three Text Inputs for memorable dates instead of a Date Input.
- [Time Input](/docs/components-forms-time-input--docs) – the counterpart for entering a time.

## Design tokens

<DesignTokensTable tokens={tokens} />

components-forms-date-picker--docs.name: Docs
components-forms-date-picker--docs.title: Components/Forms/Date Picker
components-forms-date-picker--docs.content:
{/* @license CC0-1.0 */}

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/date-picker.tokens.json";

import * as DatePickerStories from "./DatePicker.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={DatePickerStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={DatePickerStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

**Note**: Some props are excluded from the controls panel: `mode`, `onChange`, and `value` are managed by the story’s state wrapper; `defaultMonth`, `isDateDisabled`, `maxDate`, and `minDate` have no suitable control widget for their type.
The `dir` and the navigation and accessible-name labels are read-only and follow `locale`, so the controls show a fully localised Date Picker; set them yourself in your app.

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Date Picker when someone needs to choose a date or date range from a visible calendar, for example to book an appointment.

### When not to use

- Use a [Date Input](/docs/components-forms-date-input--docs) when the user knows the date and can type it into a form field.
- Use a [Calendar](/docs/components-navigation-calendar--docs) to browse content grouped by date, such as an events calendar.

### How to use

The Date Picker is a controlled component: it keeps no selection of its own.
Pass the current selection with `value` and update it in the `onChange` handler.

In the default single mode, `value` is a `Date` or `null` and `onChange` receives the picked date.
In range mode, set `mode="range"`; `value` is a `DateRange` (`{ start, end }`) and `onChange` receives the updated range.
The first pick sets the start, the second sets the end, and picking before the start begins a new range.

If you set `minDate` or `maxDate`, ensure the initial `value` falls within those bounds.
The component does not clamp or validate the incoming value.

#### Localisation

The Date Picker renders weekday names, the month caption, and the accessible date labels in the language of `locale`, which defaults to `nl-NL`.
It does not translate the rest: set `nextMonthButtonLabel`, `nextYearButtonLabel`, `previousMonthButtonLabel`, and `previousYearButtonLabel` in the same language, or they stay Dutch and screen readers announce a mix.
In range mode, also localise `rangeStartAccessibleName` and `rangeEndAccessibleName`; they are appended to the start and end dates when those are announced.
For right-to-left scripts such as Arabic, also add `dir="rtl"`; this mirrors the layout and the navigation chevrons.
Try the `locale` control above to preview each language; see the [localisation developer guide](/docs/docs-developer-guide-localisation--docs) for the tested locales.

If your app uses Date Picker in multiple places with the same language, a small wrapper component avoids repeating these props:

```tsx
import type { DatePickerProps } from "@amsterdam/design-system-react";

import { DatePicker } from "@amsterdam/design-system-react";

const ArabicDatePicker = (props: DatePickerProps) => (
  <DatePicker
    dir="rtl"
    locale="ar-MA"
    nextMonthButtonLabel="الشهر التالي"
    nextYearButtonLabel="السنة التالية"
    previousMonthButtonLabel="الشهر السابق"
    previousYearButtonLabel="السنة السابقة"
    rangeEndAccessibleName="تاريخ النهاية"
    rangeStartAccessibleName="تاريخ البداية"
    {...props}
  />
);
```

## Examples

### Range

Set `mode="range"` to let users pick a start and end date.
The Date Picker itself does not communicate that a range is expected.
Use a label, heading, or instruction to make this clear.

The user picks the start date first.
A second click on a later date completes the range; clicking the same date completes a one-day range.
Clicking a date before the current start discards the selection and begins a new range from that date.
Any click after the range is complete starts over.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Range} />

### Disabled dates

Pass `isDateDisabled` to prevent selection of specific dates, such as ones that are unavailable.
Disabled dates remain reachable with the keyboard and are announced, but they cannot be selected.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.DisabledDates} />

### Within-month bounds

Use `minDate` and `maxDate` to bound the selectable period.
Dates outside the range cannot be selected, and the month and year navigation buttons stop at the edges of the range.

When the bounds fall within the current month, dates outside them appear disabled: they are struck through and cannot be selected, but remain reachable by keyboard.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.WithinMonthBounds} />

### Limited to one month

When `minDate` and `maxDate` align with month edges, all dates remain selectable.
Only the navigation buttons are disabled.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.LimitedToOneMonth} />

## Features

### Keyboard navigation

The day grid follows the [WAI-ARIA grid pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/).
Arrow keys move between days, Home and End jump to the start and end of the week, and Page Up and Page Down move between months; hold Shift for years.
Enter or Space selects the focused day.
Moving past the end of a month shows the adjacent month and keeps focus on the day.

### Custom navigation icons

Different navigation icons can be used through the `*ButtonIcon` props, which each take the same value as the [Icon](/docs/components-media-icon--docs) component’s `svg` prop.
Websites for the City of Amsterdam must use the default icons.
For right-to-left scripts, give a custom icon a `data-directional="true"` attribute so it mirrors like the default chevrons; see the [localisation developer guide](/docs/docs-developer-guide-localisation--docs).

## Design

The Date Picker is intentionally an inline component: the calendar sits directly in the page, not in a dropdown or popover opened from a field or button.
Finding the optimal date is a focused task for the user; placing it directly on the page makes it easier to use and gives it the space and attention it deserves.
If the layout truly has no room, placing the Date Picker inside a modal [Dialog](/docs/components-containers-dialog--docs) is an acceptable last resort.

A date that falls outside the bounds is struck through rather than removed or greyed into the background.
It keeps its place in the grid, so the shape of the month stays intact and the reason a date cannot be chosen is visible rather than inferred from a gap.

The grid shows only the days of the month on view; the first week is padded with blank cells rather than the previous month’s tail.
Our palette has no comfortable way to mark another month’s dates as secondary, and without that a second set of the same day numbers — two 1sts, two 30ths — would confuse more than it clarifies.
Showing them would also raise a question the inline grid is better without: if someone picked a day carried in from a neighbouring month, should the grid jump to that month? Leaving those days out avoids it.

## Accessibility

The grid takes its accessible name from the visible month caption, so screen readers announce which month is shown.
Each day button is labelled with its full date, including the weekday, so a day number is never read out of context.
In range mode, the start and end dates are announced as such; override `rangeStartAccessibleName` and `rangeEndAccessibleName` to localise these.

Dates that cannot be chosen stay reachable with the keyboard and are still announced.
Someone moving through the month therefore learns which days are unavailable instead of finding the grid silently skip over them.

The month names, weekday names and spoken dates follow `locale`, while the navigation labels do not.
‘Localisation’ under ‘How to use’ lists the ones you have to set yourself, and leaving them unset is what produces the mix of two languages a screen reader would read out.

## See also

- [Date Input](/docs/components-forms-date-input--docs) – lets the user type a known date into a form field.
- [Calendar](/docs/components-navigation-calendar--docs) – displays content organised by date in a month view.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/error-message.tokens.json";

import * as ErrorMessageStories from "./ErrorMessage.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={ErrorMessageStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={ErrorMessageStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Show an Error Message above a form field that has a validation error.
For guidance and examples on using error messages in a form,
refer to the [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) and [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) documentation.

Read the documentation by [NL Design System](https://www.nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/foutmeldingen) and [Gov.uk](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-message/) for more information on the contents of error messages and when to show them.

### How to use

#### No rich text

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in an Error Message.
Some screen readers, like VoiceOver, skip over rich text when reading out descriptions.
For more information, see [NL Design System](https://nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/descriptions/inhoud/).

Connect the Error Message to the input it describes through the input's `aria-describedby` attribute.

### How to write

Explain what went wrong and how to fix it.

## Examples

### Custom prefix

Error messages are automatically prefixed with a visually hidden text, the Dutch word ‘Invoerfout’.
This makes the error message more clear for screen reader users.
If you want to change this prefix, to support another language for example, you can use the `prefix` prop.

<Canvas of={ErrorMessageStories.CustomPrefix} />

### With custom icon

Replace the icon with another to use Error Message in a different theme or visual identity.
Websites for the City of Amsterdam must use the default icon.

<Canvas of={ErrorMessageStories.WithCustomIcon} />

## Design

An Error Message is red text with an icon before it, and nothing else: no background, no border, no box.
The [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) around it is what marks the error more heavily, with a red rule along its leading edge, so the message itself can stay quiet.

The icon keeps the message from depending on its colour alone, which is what a reader who does not distinguish red from the text around it needs.

## Accessibility

An Error Message renders a `p` element, so it is read as ordinary text when the field it describes is reached through `aria-describedby`.

It opens with a word that is in the markup and hidden visually — ‘Invoerfout’ by default.
A description read out on its own gives no clue that it is an error, so the prefix supplies the context that the colour and the icon carry visually.

The component does not announce itself when it appears, and it is not a live region.
Announcing it is the job of the field that now describes it, or of an [Invalid Form Alert](/docs/components-forms-invalid-form-alert--docs) at the top of the form.

## See also

- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a single input with its Label, description, and Error Message.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – wraps a group of inputs with a shared Error Message.
- [Invalid Form Alert](/docs/components-forms-invalid-form-alert--docs) – summarises all form errors at the top of the page.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/field.tokens.json";

import * as FieldStories from "./Field.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={FieldStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={FieldStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Field to wrap a single input together with its Label, description, and Error Message.

### When not to use

Use [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) to wrap multiple inputs.

### How to use

#### No rich text

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in descriptions.
Some screen readers, like VoiceOver, skip over rich text when reading out descriptions.
For more information, see [NL Design System](https://nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/descriptions/inhoud/).

Connect each related element to the input through `aria-describedby` so screen readers announce them.

## Examples

### With description

A Field can have a description.
Make sure to connect this description to the input in the Field,
otherwise it won’t be read by a screen reader.
Add an `aria-describedby` attribute to the input and provide the `id` of the describing element as its value.

<Canvas of={FieldStories.WithDescription} />

### With validation

A Field can indicate if the contained input has a validation error.
Use an [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) to describe the error.
Make sure to connect the Error Message to the input in the Field,
otherwise it won’t be read by a screen reader.
Add an `aria-describedby` attribute to the input and provide the `id` of Error Message as its value.

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in an Error Message. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs#no-rich-text).

<Canvas of={FieldStories.WithValidation} />

### In a Field Set

Fields can be nested inside a Field Set.
Use the `inFieldSet` prop on the Labels of the Fields to show them in a lighter style.

<Canvas of={FieldStories.InAFieldSet} />

## Features

There’s no need to add white space between the children of a Field.
The component does this automatically.

## Design

The spacing between the children of a Field is not uniform.
Everything sits a small distance apart, except the element directly before an Error Message, which gets more room.
The message is then read as belonging to the field below it rather than to the description above it.

Browsers that cannot express that condition fall back to the same small gap everywhere, which is acceptable: the order still reads correctly, only the emphasis is lost.

An invalid Field is marked by a red rule along its leading edge and indented away from it.
The whole question shifts, so the error is visible while scanning a long form rather than only when reading the field itself.

In print, a Field is never split across two pages.

## Accessibility

A Field renders a `div` with no role of its own and adds nothing to the accessibility tree.
It groups its parts visually, and nothing more.

This is why ‘How to use’ insists on `aria-describedby`: the description and the Error Message are related to the input by that attribute alone, not by sitting inside the same Field.
Someone reading the field on its own would otherwise get the label and nothing else.

The red rule marking an invalid Field is not announced either, and neither is the colour of the Error Message.
The hidden prefix inside the message is what says that something went wrong.

## See also

- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – wraps multiple inputs.
- [Label](/docs/components-forms-label--docs) – names the input inside the Field.
- [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) – describes a validation error for the input.

components-forms-field-set--docs.content: {/* @license CC0-1.0 */} import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks"; import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable"; import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/field-set.tokens.json"; import * as FieldSetStories from "./FieldSet.stories.tsx"; <Description of={FieldSetStories} /> <Primary /> <Controls /> ## Usage guidelines ### When to use Group a collection of [Radio](/docs/components-forms-radio--docs) buttons or [Checkboxes](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) into a Field Set. This allows them to share a label, description, and error message, while each option still has its own label. A Field Set can also express the relation between a group of inputs or other controls. For instance, you might want to group several text inputs into one Field Set when requesting an address or various parts of a name. ### When not to use Use a [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) to wrap a single input instead. ### How to use Mark a Field Set as `optional` only for a list of Radios or Checkboxes, and if selecting any option is not necessary. ## Examples ### With description A Field Set can have a description. Make sure to connect this description to the Field Set or a specific input, otherwise this won’t be read by a screen reader. Add an `aria-describedby` attribute to the Field Set and provide the `id` of the describing element as its value. Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in descriptions. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-field--docs#no-rich-text). <Canvas of={FieldSetStories.WithDescription} /> ### With Hint A Field Set can indicate whether all of the inputs it contains are optional or required. Make sure to add `aria-required` to <em>all</em> form elements in the Field Set when they are required. <Canvas of={FieldSetStories.WithHint} /> ### With Validation A Field Set can indicate whether any of the inputs it contains has a validation error. Use an [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) to describe the error. Make sure to connect the Error Message to the correct input in the Field Set, otherwise it won’t be read by a screen reader. Add an `aria-describedby` attribute to the input and provide the `id` of Error Message as its value. Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in an Error Message. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs#no-rich-text). <Canvas of={FieldSetStories.WithValidation} /> ### With Heading in Legend If the Field Set holds the only question on the page, its Legend serves as the main heading as well. Set `legendIsPageHeading` to include an `h1` element to reflect this. <Canvas of={FieldSetStories.WithHeadingInLegend} /> ### With a nested Field Set A Field Set can be nested inside another Field Set. Use the `inFieldSet` prop to show the legend in a lighter style. <Canvas of={FieldSetStories.WithANestedFieldSet} /> ## Features There’s no need to add white space between the children of a Field Set. The component does this automatically. ## Design The spacing between the children of a Field Set climbs in four steps. Ordinary children sit close together; the element before an Error Message gets more room; the element before a nested Field or Field Set more again; and two of those in a row are furthest apart. Depth in a form is expressed by white space rather than by boxes or rules, so the more a Field Set holds, the more clearly its parts separate. Browsers that cannot express those conditions fall back to the smallest gap everywhere, which is acceptable: the order still reads correctly, only the grouping is flatter. The legend loses the notch a browser normally cuts for it in the border, because there is no border to cut. It is laid out so that a border would pass around it rather than through it, which keeps the option open for a theme that draws one. An invalid Field Set is marked by a red rule along its leading edge and indented away from it, the same way a [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) is. A Field Set does not grow to fit an input that asks for a width of its own, such as a Text Input with a `size` attribute. Without that, a single wide field would stretch the whole group and the layout around it. In print, a Field Set is never split across two pages. ## Accessibility A Field Set has the implicit ARIA role `group`. Set `role="radiogroup"` when it groups [Radio](/docs/components-forms-radio--docs) buttons, so that screen readers announce it as a radio group. That role also permits `aria-required` on the Field Set, which the `group` role does not allow. The legend names that group, and screen readers repeat it before each option inside it. Someone moving from one Radio to the next therefore hears which question they are answering, not just the answer they are on. `legendIsPageHeading` wraps the legend in an `h1` rather than replacing it, so the same words serve as the heading of the page and as the name of the group. ## See also - [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a single input. - [Radio](/docs/components-forms-radio--docs) – one of the inputs typically grouped in a Field Set. - [Checkbox](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) – one of the inputs typically grouped in a Field Set. ## Design tokens <DesignTokensTable tokens={tokens} />

<Meta of={FileInputStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={FileInputStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a File Input when users need to attach one or more files from their device.

### How to use

Wrap a File Input in a Field to associate it with a Label and description.

## Examples

### Multiple files

Allow multiple files to be selected.
The label will update to show the number of files selected.

<Canvas of={FileInputStories.MultipleFiles} />

### Restrict file types

Limit the types of files that can be selected.
Some examples are `image/*`, `video/*`, or `audio/*`.
To limit to a specific file type, use the MIME type, such as `application/pdf`.

- [MDN File Input](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/file#limiting_accepted_file_types): More examples

<Canvas of={FileInputStories.RestrictFileTypes} />

### Disabled

<Canvas of={FileInputStories.Disabled} />

### In a Field

Use a Field component to group a File Input with a Label and possibly a description.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Text Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={FileInputStories.InAField} />

## Design

The filename label and button are displayed in the language of the browser and can vary between browsers and operating systems.

The field itself gets the border, padding and type of the other form fields, and the button the browser draws inside it is restyled to look like a secondary [Button](/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).
Hovering thickens that button’s outline with an inset ring rather than a wider border, so nothing beside it moves.

The button takes the type of the field around it rather than setting its own.
Browsers give a file selector button a font of their own, and inheriting it is what keeps the control from looking like a piece of another interface.

## Accessibility

A File Input renders a native `input` of type file, so the file dialog, the keyboard behaviour and the list of chosen files all come from the browser and the operating system.

Both the button’s wording and the text stating what has been selected are generated by the browser, in the browser’s language rather than the page’s.
A visitor on a page in one language may hear that text in another, and nothing the page does can change it.

A [File List](/docs/components-forms-file-list--docs) beside the field is how a page states the selection in its own words and gives the user a way to remove a file.

## See also

- [File List](/docs/components-forms-file-list--docs) – shows the files that the user has selected.
- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a File Input with its Label and description.

## Subcomponents

### Item

Represents a selected `file`.
Provide an `onDelete` callback to let users remove it from the list.

<Canvas of={FileListItemStories.Item} />

<Controls of={FileListItemStories.Item} />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a File List to display the files a user has selected or uploaded, showing each file’s name, type, size, and a preview.

## Examples

### Using a file input

To connect a File Input to a File List, use the `onChange` event to update the
list of files and use `onDelete` when removing a file from the list.

<Canvas of={FileListStories.WithInput} />

<Source code={FileInputWithFileList} language="jsx" />

## Design

Every item is one row: a preview of fixed width, then the name and details, then the delete button.
The preview column is the same width whether it holds a thumbnail or the generic document icon, so the names line up down the list.

A name too long for its row is cut off with an ellipsis on a single line rather than wrapped.
Rows then stay the same height whatever has been uploaded, which keeps a list of several files scannable.

The file type and size sit below the name in their own colour, so the name stays the thing you read first.

## Accessibility

A File List renders `ul` and `li` elements, so screen readers announce it as a list and report how many files it holds.

Cutting off a long name is visual only.
The whole name is in the markup and is announced in full, so nothing is lost to someone who cannot see where the row ends.

The preview of an image file repeats the file name as its alternative text, so that name is announced twice: once for the thumbnail and once for the text beside it.

Every delete button is labelled ‘Verwijder’, in Dutch and without the name of the file it removes.
Someone reviewing the buttons of the page out of context hears the same word for each of them, and the label cannot be configured.
Until it can, prefer a File List short enough to keep each button next to the file it belongs to.

## See also

- [File Input](/docs/components-forms-file-input--docs) – lets the user select files to add to the File List.

import { Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/invalid-form-alert.tokens.json";

import * as InvalidFormAlertStories from "./InvalidFormAlert.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={InvalidFormAlertStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={InvalidFormAlertStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Always show an Invalid Form Alert when there is a validation error, even if there’s only one.

### How to use

You must link the errors in the Invalid Form Alert to the answer they relate to.

For questions that require a user to answer using a single field, like a file upload, select, textarea or text input, link to the `id` of that field.

When a user has to enter their answer into multiple fields, such as day, month and year fields, link to the `id` of the first field that contains an error.
If you do not know which field contains an error, link to the `id` of the first field.

For questions that require a user to select one or more options from a list using Radios or Checkboxes, link to the `id` of the first Radio or Checkbox.

Each `id` becomes the `href` of a link, so it needs a leading number sign (`#`).

Put the Invalid Form Alert directly above the first question on the page.
Place it outside of the `<form>`-tag, [to make sure screen readers do not skip it](https://nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/meerdere-stappen/#plaats-de-informatie-over-waar-de-gebruiker-is-in-de-stappen-boven-het-formulier).

The heading level of the Invalid Form Alert depends on where in the page it is placed; this may differ per page.

## Features

This component adds the error count to the document title,
in line with [GOV.UK guidelines for informing users about validation errors](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/validation/#how-to-tell-the-user-about-validation-errors).

This component receives focus the first time it gets displayed on a page.
This allows keyboard users to quickly navigate to the errors in the form.
It also scrolls the component into view if it isn’t already.
Note: this functionality has been disabled on this page, to prevent unexpected focus behaviour.

## Design

An Invalid Form Alert is an [Alert](/docs/components-feedback-alert--docs) holding a [Link List](/docs/components-navigation-link-list--docs), rather than a component with a look of its own.
A reader who has met the red Alert elsewhere on the site recognises it here, and the errors read as what they are: a list of links to the questions that need attention.

The component renders nothing at all when there are no errors, so a form needs no condition around it.

## Accessibility

The Alert is focused the first time it appears and scrolled into view, which moves a keyboard user straight to the summary instead of leaving them where they submitted from.
It is given a negative tab index so that it can be focused this way without becoming a stop that everyone has to pass on every later visit to the form.

Each error is a link to the field it concerns, so following one moves focus into the form at the question that needs answering.
This is what ‘How to use’ is protecting when it asks for the `id` of the first field of a group: a link to the group as a whole would land nowhere in particular.

The error count is added to the document title as well.
A screen reader announces the title when a page loads or a route changes, so someone who submits a form and lands back on it hears that something went wrong before reading anything.

Placing the component outside the `form` element, as ‘How to use’ asks, is what keeps some screen readers from skipping it in their forms mode.

## See also

- [Error Message](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs) – the per-field message linked from the Invalid Form Alert.
- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a single input with its Label, description, and Error Message.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – wraps a group of inputs with a shared Error Message.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/label.tokens.json";

import * as LabelStories from "./Label.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={LabelStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={LabelStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Always associate a form element (such as an `input` or `textarea`) with a Label.

### How to use

Set `optional` to `true` if the input is not required.
Use `hint` to show a custom hint text.

Mark the optional fields rather than the required ones, as [the NL Design System guideline on required fields](https://nldesignsystem.nl/richtlijnen/formulieren/voorkom-fouten/verplichte-velden/) recommends.
A form should ask only what it needs, so most of its fields are required.
Mark the required fields instead when most fields are optional.

Despite its name, `inFieldSet` has no structural effect: it only changes how the Label and its hint look.

## Examples

### Optional

Use the `optional` prop to indicate that the user doesn’t need to fill in the field to submit the form.

<Canvas of={LabelStories.Optional} />

### With hint

Use the `hint` prop to either customize the text for the optional property or provide another type of remark.

Note: ensure the hint meets [language level B1](https://www.amsterdam.nl/schrijfwijzer/heldere-taal-basis-onze-huisstijl/).
For the same reason, the default hint text in Dutch is ‘niet verplicht’, not ‘optioneel’.

<Canvas of={LabelStories.WithHint} />

### With Heading

If the parent Field holds the only question on the page, its Label serves as the main heading as well.
Set `isPageHeading` to include an `h1` element to reflect this.

<Canvas of={LabelStories.WithHeading} />

### In a Field Set

When a Label is used in a Field inside a Field Set, use the `inFieldSet` prop to show it in a lighter style.

<Canvas of={LabelStories.InAFieldSet} />

## Design

A Label is set in bold, at the size of a level 3 Heading and with the tighter line height that goes with it.
A question in a form is treated as a small heading, because that is what it is: the thing a reader scans for when working out what is being asked.

Inside a Field Set that weight drops to regular.
The legend then carries the emphasis for the group, and the labels of the individual options read as answers rather than as questions of their own.

A Label that runs onto more than one line has its line lengths balanced, so it never ends on a single short word above the field.

## Accessibility

A Label renders a `label` element tied to its input, so activating the label moves focus to the field and a screen reader announces the label when the field is reached.

The hint is written inside the label.
It becomes part of the accessible name of the field, which is what makes ‘niet verplicht’ reach someone who never sees it beside the text.

`isPageHeading` wraps the label in an `h1` rather than replacing it.
The text then serves as the heading of the page and as the name of the field at once, so navigating by heading and reaching the input both produce the same words.

## See also

- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a single input together with its Label.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – uses a legend instead of a Label to name a group of inputs.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/password-input.tokens.json";

import * as PasswordInputStories from "./PasswordInput.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={PasswordInputStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={PasswordInputStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use this component when the input requires sensitive information, like passwords or PINs.
It ensures that the input is not readable by others who might be looking at the screen.

### How to use

Consider setting the following attributes:

1. Allow the user’s password manager to automatically fill the password through `autocomplete="current-password"`.
   When asking for a new password, use `autocomplete="new-password"` instead.
2. Do not add a `minlength` attribute to ensure passwords meet a minimum length requirement.
   This would prematurely indicate an error to the user – while they are still typing.
3. Do not add a `maxlength` attribute either.
   Users will not get any feedback when their text input has been truncated, e.g. after pasting from a password manager.
4. If the password is a numeric PIN, add `inputmode="numeric"`.
   Devices with virtual keyboards then switch to a numeric keypad layout which makes entering the password easier.

Follow the [guidelines for asking for passwords](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/passwords/) of the GOV.UK Design System.

Wrap a Password Input in a Field to associate it with a Label, description, and Error Message.

## Examples

### Size

Match the width of the input to the expected length of its content.
Use the `size` attribute for this.
The input won’t grow beyond the width of its container.

<Canvas of={PasswordInputStories.Size} />

### In a Field

Use a Field to group a Password Input with a Label, description and / or an Error Message.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Password Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={PasswordInputStories.InAField} />

### In a Field with validation

If the Password Input can become invalid, add an Error Message and its `id` to the `aria-describedby` attribute of the Password Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={PasswordInputStories.InAFieldWithValidation} />

## Features

The characters entered are hidden, represented by squares.

This component sets `autocorrect="off"` and `spellcheck="false"` to stop browsers automatically changing user input.
Passwords shouldn’t be checked for spelling or grammar.
This may also prevent posting the password to third-party plugins.
These props cannot be overridden.

## Design

A Password Input is identical to a [Text Input](/docs/components-forms-text-input--docs) in every respect a stylesheet controls: the same border, padding, type, width behaviour, and invalid and disabled states.
Only the masking marks it as different, and the browser draws that.

There is no control to reveal what has been typed.
The component is the field and nothing more, so a service that wants a reveal button builds it beside the field rather than receiving one it cannot remove.

## Accessibility

A Password Input renders an `input` of type password, so the browser masks the value, keeps it out of autofill for ordinary fields, and lets a password manager recognise it.

Its text direction is set to follow what is typed rather than the direction of the page.
A password made of characters from another script is then displayed the way it was entered instead of being reordered around it.

The `invalid` prop sets `aria-invalid` on the field, and that styling responds to the browser’s own `:invalid` state as well.
A password is incomplete for most of the time it is being typed, so a `required` or `pattern` attribute would mark the field red throughout; leave the state to your own validation and set it through `invalid`.

## See also

- [Text Input](/docs/components-forms-text-input--docs) – for non-sensitive single-line text.
- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a Password Input with its Label, description, and Error Message.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/radio.tokens.json";

import * as RadioStories from "./Radio.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={RadioStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={RadioStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Radio when the user must select exactly one option from a list.

### When not to use

Use a [Checkbox](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) when a user can select more than 1 option from a list.

Do not assume that users will know how many options they can select based on the visual difference between Radios and Checkboxes alone.
If needed, add a hint explaining this, for example, ‘Select one option’.

### How to use

Order Radios alphabetically by default.
In some cases, it can be helpful to order them from most-to-least common options.
For example, you could order options for ‘Where do you live?’ based on population size.
However you should do this with extreme caution as it can reinforce bias.
If in doubt, order alphabetically.

Do not check a Radio initially.
This prevents users from leaving the question unanswered.
It also increases the chance of submitting a wrong answer.

Wrap a list of Radios in a Field Set so they share a legend and any description or Error Message.

When a group of Radios fails validation, set `invalid` on every Radio in it.
The group as a whole lacks a valid answer; no single option is at fault.

### How to write

Labels should be concise.
Try to keep labels shorter than 4 words.

## Examples

### In a Field Set

Use a Field Set to group several Radios with a legend, description and / or an Error Message.

Add `role="radiogroup"` to the Field Set to have it explicitly announced as a radio group (the default role is just ‘group’).
The ‘radio group’ role also allows using `aria-required` on Field Set; that isn’t allowed for the ‘group’ role.
Even so, always set `aria-required` on the individual Radios as well to ensure that screen readers can read it.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Field Set.

Check [the Field Set docs](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.InAFieldSet} />

### In a Field Set with validation

A Field Set with a Radio group can become invalid.
In this case, connect an Error Message to the Field Set.
Add an `aria-describedby` attribute to the Field Set and provide the `id` of Error Message as its value.

Do not use rich text (such as links or lists) in an Error Message. [Find out why](/docs/components-forms-error-message--docs#no-rich-text).

Check [the Field Set docs](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.InAFieldSetWithValidation} />

### With custom icon

Replace the icon with a custom version to use the Radio in a different theme or visual identity.
Use `ams-radio__circle`, `ams-radio__hover-indicator` and `ams-radio__checked-indicator` classes in its SVG markup.
Websites for the City of Amsterdam must use the default icon.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.WithCustomIcon} />

## Design

The circle is drawn as an SVG inside the label rather than by the browser, which is what makes a custom icon possible at all and keeps the control identical across browsers.
It carries a separate ring that appears on hover, so the circle grows a halo instead of changing size or colour.

A Radio is round and a [Checkbox](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) is square, which is the only thing distinguishing one from the other at a glance.
That difference is easy to miss, which is why ‘When not to use’ asks for a hint saying how many options may be chosen rather than trusting the shape to say it.

In forced colours mode the drawing is redone in system colours, since the fills the tokens set are ignored there.

## Accessibility

A Radio renders a native `input` inside a `label`, so the whole label is the target and the browser supplies the role, the checked state, and the arrow-key behaviour that moves between the options of a group.

The input is not hidden away: it is reduced to no width, which keeps it focusable, announced, and submitted with the form.
Its focus ring is moved onto the label so the ring surrounds the circle and its text rather than a control with no size.

A group of Radios takes one stop in the tab order, and the arrow keys move within it.
That is browser behaviour tied to the shared `name`, so give every Radio in a group the same one.

Marking every Radio in a failed group as invalid — as ‘How to use’ asks — is what puts the state on each option a screen reader reaches, since the group itself is only announced once.

## See also

- [Checkbox](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) – when a user can select more than one option.
- [Field Set](/docs/components-forms-field-set--docs) – groups several Radios with a shared legend.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/search-field.tokens.json";

import * as SearchFieldStories from "./SearchField.stories.tsx";
import * as SearchFieldButtonStories from "./SearchFieldButton.stories.tsx";
import * as SearchFieldInputStories from "./SearchFieldInput.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={SearchFieldStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={SearchFieldStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Subcomponents

A Search Field always combines an Input and a Button, as the example above shows.

### Input

The text input of the Search Field.
Its visually hidden `label` describes the field for screen readers.

<Canvas of={SearchFieldInputStories.Input} />

<Controls of={SearchFieldInputStories.Input} />

### Button

Submits the search.
It renders an icon-only Button whose `children` provide the accessible name.

<Canvas of={SearchFieldButtonStories.Button} />

<Controls of={SearchFieldButtonStories.Button} />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Search Field where the user needs to search through the content of the page or website.

### How to use

You can use `autofocus` to place focus directly on a search field when the user arrives on a page.
However, use this feature with caution, as it can have negative consequences:

- For screen reader users, this may result in skipping important content above the search field.
- On smaller devices, the use of `autofocus` may automatically scroll the page to the search field, potentially causing users to miss previous content.
- On touchscreen devices, this can trigger the keyboard to appear immediately, hiding important content.

Use `autofocus` only if the search field is at the beginning of a page and there are no other elements on a page that a user might want to interact with first.

For more information: [Accessibility Tips: Be Cautious When Using Autofocus](https://www.boia.org/blog/accessibility-tips-be-cautious-when-using-autofocus)

Provide a label that describes the purpose of the search.
There is no way to show that label: the Input always renders it visually hidden.
A placeholder is therefore the only visible text the field can carry, and it disappears on the first keystroke.

## Examples

### With placeholder

A Search Field can have a placeholder text.

<Canvas of={SearchFieldStories.WithPlaceholder} />

### Disabled

Set `disabled` on the Search Field to make both the Input and the Button unavailable.
Neither of them can enable themselves, so the two always match.

<Canvas of={SearchFieldStories.Disabled} />

### Controlled component

By default, the search field is not managed by React but by the browser.
However, it can be controlled by React.
If you enter a value in this search field and use the search Button or the Enter key, you will receive a notification.

<Canvas of={SearchFieldStories.Controlled} />

## Features

Users can initiate a search by using the search button or the Enter key.

Both `autocomplete` and `spellcheck` are turned off by default.
These features can be disruptive for a user searching for part of a word, and `autocomplete` may interfere with an Autosuggest component.

## Design

The input and the button are flush against one another and read as a single control, with the input taking whatever width is left over.

A focused input lifts itself above the button so its focus ring is drawn in full rather than cut off where the two meet.
That lift is contained within the component, so it can never end up in front of anything else on the page.

The browser’s own button for clearing the field is restyled with our icon where a browser offers one, and greyed along with the rest when the field is disabled.

In print, the field keeps its background colour instead of being flattened to save ink.

## Accessibility

The component uses `role="search"` for the search landmark role.
It is a real `form`, so pressing Enter in the field submits it the way any form does, and assistive technology lists the search among the landmarks of the page.

The label of the Input is always rendered visually hidden.
It names the field for anyone who cannot see where it sits, which is why ‘How to use’ asks for a label that describes what is being searched rather than the word ‘Search’.

The Button is icon-only and takes its accessible name from its `children`, so the magnifier is never announced as an unlabelled control.

Disabling the Search Field disables both parts, and neither can enable itself again.
The two can therefore never be announced in different states.

## See also

- [Text Input](/docs/components-forms-text-input--docs) – for free-text input that isn’t a search.

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

<Meta of={SelectStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={SelectStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Subcomponents

Provide the choices of the Select with Option subcomponents, and group related choices with a Group.
They render the native `<option>` and `<optgroup>` elements and accept their standard attributes only.

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Select when the user must pick one option from a list that is too long to display as Radios.

### When not to use

Avoid adding functionality to allow selecting multiple options.
Multi select is harder to use on desktop as they require the user to hold down the `Ctrl` or `Cmd` key while clicking on the options.
It is recommended to use checkboxes instead.

### How to use

Wrap a Select in a Field to associate it with a Label, description, and Error Message.

## Examples

### Grouped

Use the `Select.Group` component to group options.
The component requires a `label` attribute.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Grouped} />

### Invalid

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Invalid} />

### Disabled

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Disabled} />

### In a Field

Use a Field to group a Select with a Label, description and / or an Error Message.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Select.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.InAField} />

### In a Field with validation

If the Select can become invalid, add an Error Message and its `id` to the `aria-describedby` attribute of the Select.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.InAFieldWithValidation} />

## Design

A Select shares its border, padding, type and states with a [Text Input](/docs/components-forms-text-input--docs), so a field the user types into and one they choose from sit level in the same form.

The chevron browsers draw is replaced by one of ours, and the field reserves room for it at the end so a long option never runs underneath.
It is drawn three times over — in the interactive blue, in the hover blue, and in grey when disabled — because a background image cannot take the colour of the text the way an icon in the markup would.

A Select showing several options at once keeps the native appearance and no chevron, since there is nothing to expand.

## Accessibility

A Select renders a native `select` element with native `option` and `optgroup` elements inside it.
The list that opens is the operating system’s own, so it behaves the way every other menu on that device does: the same keys, the same gestures, and the same behaviour with a screen reader, none of which the design system reimplements.

That is also the reason the appearance stops at the closed field.
An open list cannot be styled, and replacing it with markup we could style would mean rebuilding all of that behaviour.

A disabled option is greyed but still announced, so the user hears that a choice exists and is unavailable rather than not hearing it at all.

## See also

- [Checkbox](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) – use for multi-select interactions instead of a multi-Select.
- [Radio](/docs/components-forms-radio--docs) – for short lists where one option must be selected.
- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a Select with its Label, description, and Error Message.

## Design tokens

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/switch.tokens.json";

<Meta of={SwitchStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={SwitchStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Switch to toggle between two different states.
It is a binary action.
The action takes place immediately when the user operates the switch.

### How to use

A Switch must have a label, and in most cases, this label should be visible.

## Examples

### With Label

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.WithLabel} />

## Design

The track and the thumb are the whole of a Switch: a rounded bar with a circle that slides from one end to the other, and a colour change behind it.
There is no text inside it, so it needs no room for words in either state and stays the same width whichever way it is set.

The thumb moves by exactly the width of the track minus its borders, so it comes to rest flush against the end rather than at a distance measured separately for each size.

The slide and the colour change behind the thumb are animated only for users who have not asked for reduced motion.
Everyone else sees the new state at once, with no travel across the track.

The track carries a transparent border rather than none at all.
In forced colours mode a background is replaced by the system’s own, and the border is what remains to give the Switch an outline; a floor of one pixel keeps a theme from removing it by setting the token to zero.

Hovering puts a shadow around the thumb rather than moving or resizing it.

## Accessibility

A Switch renders a checkbox marked as a switch, so it is announced as on or off rather than as checked or unchecked, and it is operated with Space like any other checkbox.

The visible track is an empty `label` that supplies no name.
A Switch therefore takes its name from a [Label](/docs/components-forms-label--docs) tied to it with `htmlFor`, which is what ‘How to use’ asks for; without one it is announced as an unnamed switch.

The input is not hidden away: it is reduced to no width, which keeps it focusable, announced, and submitted with the form.
Its focus ring is moved onto the track so the ring surrounds the switch rather than a control with no size.

## See also

- [Checkbox](/docs/components-forms-checkbox--docs) – when the choice is part of a form rather than an instant setting.

## Design tokens

import { Canvas, Controls, Description, Meta, Primary, Title } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

import { DesignTokensTable } from "#storybook/_components/DesignTokensTable/DesignTokensTable";
import tokens from "#tokens/components/ams/text-area.tokens.json";

import * as TextAreaStories from "./TextArea.stories.tsx";

<Meta of={TextAreaStories} />

<Title />

<Description of={TextAreaStories} />

<Primary />

<Controls />

## Usage guidelines

### When to use

Use a Text Area when users need to enter more than 1 sentence of text, such as a comment or description.

### How to use

The height of the Text Area should be appropriate for the information to be entered.

Use `spellcheck="false"` for fields that may contain sensitive information, such as passwords and personal data.
Some browser extensions for spell-checking send this information to external servers.

A Text Area must have a label, and in most cases, this label should be visible.

## Examples

### Vertical resize

<Canvas of={TextAreaStories.VerticalResize} />

### Horizontal resize

<Canvas of={TextAreaStories.HorizontalResize} />

### No resize

<Canvas of={TextAreaStories.NoResize} />

### Invalid

<Canvas of={TextAreaStories.Invalid} />

### Disabled

<Canvas of={TextAreaStories.Disabled} />

### In a Field

Use a Field to group a Text Area with a Label, description and / or an Error Message.

If you don’t need the description, remove its Paragraph and the `aria-describedby` from the Text Input.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={TextAreaStories.InAField} />

### In a Field with validation

If the Text Area can become invalid, add an Error Message and its `id` to the `aria-describedby` prop of the Text Area.

Check [the Field docs](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) for more information on configuring it.

<Canvas of={TextAreaStories.InAFieldWithValidation} />

## Design

A Text Area shares its border, padding, type and states with a [Text Input](/docs/components-forms-text-input--docs), so a form built from both reads as one set of fields.

It has a minimum height of its own, which is what says at a glance that more than one line is expected here.
Setting `cols` switches the width from filling the container to sizing by character count, and the field still never grows past the space it has.

The `resize` prop decides which directions the user may drag.
The handle browsers put in the corner is left in place by default: it costs nothing, and it lets someone give themselves more room for a long answer without leaving the page.

## Accessibility

A Text Area renders a `textarea` element and is announced with its label and anything `aria-describedby` points at.

Resizing is a convenience for people who need more room on screen, and it is not supported in Safari on iOS.
Nothing depends on it, so a field there behaves as it would with `resize` set to none.

The invalid styling responds to `aria-invalid="true"` and to the browser’s own `:invalid` state alike, as it does for a [Text Input](/docs/components-forms-text-input--docs).

## See also

- [Text Input](/docs/components-forms-text-input--docs) – for single-line text input.
- [Character Count](/docs/components-forms-character-count--docs) – communicates a character limit on a Text Area.
- [Field](/docs/components-forms-field--docs) – wraps a Text Area with its Label, description, and Error Message.

## Design tokens
